observation_model.censoring: handled by the evaluator; the forward conditions on the flame burning at the cutoff
observation_model.endpoint: cause-specific event time; an operator or script stop is its own cause, never an extinction; self-extinction is the end of the hot flame
observation_model.prefix: prospective conditions and control stages known at the cutoff; no time series

numerics.integrator: weighted mean of the members' event tables at the requested times, over up to ten members and, when the script's planned stop is read, up to three stop times (the rules of committee2.rs); flame5.rs, flame6.rs and flame7.rs members, each the law of flame.rs, flame3.rs or flame4.rs reading its own fuel table, with its own step and constants

applicability.fuels: the rows of the release's fuel table with fuel.admit = 1 (rows: ethane, propane, butane, ethylene, methane, hydrogen); the row of a prefix is its fuel_species, else its stored indicators
applicability.interpretation: observational event prediction under the observed experimental policy; operator termination is not spontaneous extinction; extinction is the end of the hot flame
applicability.meaning: declared physical domain of the handwritten clocks, not a training-support region
applicability.population: established hot flame of a burner-stabilised gas flame (PSI-159)
applicability.time_origin: hot ignition per table 'burn time (sec)' (not adjudicated against logs)

lineage_note: F1 of the third committee spec for inverse flames: the adopted acme_inverse.wsp5 P1 (the carried law with weight 2 and the hold scenario with weight 1) with every member reading the fuel from the typed table F1. Identical to P1 on ethane, p

checks.detail: forward sources name no fitting, sampling or random routine; ignis-wsp links no optimizer crate (tests/strict.rs checks the dependency graph)
synthetic fixture prefix: 41 forecast times, valid finite artifact
